plan: Reduce exposure to SPY to 20% to lower concentration.
Increase QQQI to 20% to boost income holdings.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.

conservative.read: This plan aims for capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged ETFs and high-beta names, holding a larger cash buffer. Expect lower drawdowns but also capped upside potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to address concentration.
Reduce QQQI to 20% to balance income and growth.
Increase CRWD to 15% to lean into a strong performer.
Maintain minimal exposure to leveraged ETFs SOXL (2%) and SPAL (1%).
Sell METU to zero and trim MSFU to 1% to reduce high-beta software risk.
This plan seeks a balance between growth and risk management.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets around 2.5% monthly return by managing risk first. It reduces concentration, trims leverage, and slightly increases exposure to a strong performer while maintaining a moderate cash buffer. Expect moderate growth with controlled drawdowns.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to manage concentration.
Reduce QQQI to 10% to free up capital for growth.
Increase CRWD to 15% to double down on a strong performer.
Add to leveraged ETFs SOXL (to 5%) and SPAL (to 3%).
Initiate new positions in inverse ETFs TECS (5%), SQQQ (5%), and TZA (5%) for potential downside capture.
This plan aggressively pursues growth through concentration and leverage.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% monthly return by embracing leverage and concentration. It increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and adds inverse ETFs for potential rapid gains, but carries significantly higher risk of large drawdowns and leverage decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Trim SPY to 20% to prioritize income generation.
Increase QQQI to 30% to maximize income holdings.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Sell all high-beta software (METU, MSFU, PLTU) and leveraged semis (MUU) to zero.
This plan focuses on generating steady monthly distributions.
It aims for low drawdowns and reliable income over aggressive growth.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly return through distributions. It shifts heavily into income-generating assets like QQQI, cuts all leverage and high-beta single names, and maintains a cash buffer. While prioritizing stability, NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
